text:
The change adds daily visit counts, but groups timestamps by the host’s local timezone instead of UTC. I reproduced a visit at `2026-10-10 23:00 UTC` being counted under `2026-10-11`.

Both test functions pass when called directly; pytest is unavailable. The new test misses this bug because it uses noon timestamps and checks only counts, never date keys.

      "body": "When the host uses a non-UTC timezone, visits near UTC midnight are counted under the wrong day because datetime.fromtimestamp(ts) uses local time. On the current host, 2026-10-10 23:00 UTC produces {'2026-10-11': 1} instead of {'2026-10-10': 1}. The new test uses noon timestamps and asserts only values, so it misses incorrect date keys.",
